classification.difficultyReason: Find the probability of one specified order, identify the three orders for exactly two heads, and combine outcomes or use a complement for the at-least events.

content.prompt: A biased coin with outcomes $H$ and $T$ has $P(H)=0.55$. The coin is tossed 3 times. Find the probability of obtaining

answer.short:
$\frac{3267}{8000}$

Each of the three possible orders has the same probability.
answer.worked:
The three orders $HHT$, $HTH$ and $THH$ each have probability $\frac{1089}{8000}$.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly two heads}) &= 3\times\frac{1089}{8000} \\ P(\text{exactly two heads}) &= \frac{3267}{8000}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{2299}{4000}$

Add the probabilities of exactly two heads and three heads.
answer.worked:
Exactly two heads has probability $\frac{3267}{8000}$. Three heads has probability $(\frac{11}{20})^3=\frac{1331}{8000}$.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least two heads}) &= \frac{3267}{8000}+\frac{1331}{8000} \\ P(\text{at least two heads}) &= \frac{2299}{4000}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{7271}{8000}$

Subtract the probability of three tails from 1.
answer.worked:
No heads means three tails.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one head}) &= 1-\left(\frac9{20}\right)^3 \\ P(\text{at least one head}) &= 1-\frac{729}{8000} \\ P(\text{at least one head}) &= \frac{7271}{8000}\end{align*}$$
